newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac, Juppe dip in polls after gains.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac, Juppe dip in polls after gains.

text.p: Public support for French conservative President Jacques Chirac has dipped again after a brief recovery, two opinions poll showed on Thursday.
One survey, by the Louis Harris Institute for Valeurs Actuelles magazine, said voters with a favourable impression of Chirac's performance slipped to 35 percent, down from 40 percent a month earlier.
Those with a poor impression rose to 60 percent from 54.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe's rating also declined after three months of gains with just 31 percent rating his performance good against 33 percent in March. The percentage with a bad impression climbed to 65 percent from 62.
And 64 percent reckoned that the economic and social climate was worsening in France, little changed from 65 percent the month before. Unemployment is at a record 12.8 percent.
Another poll, by IPSOS for weekly Le Point, showed approval for Chirac slipped two percentage points to 37 percent while disapproval rose by two points to 55 percent.
The monthly IPSOS survey showed a similar result for Juppe, with his approval rating falling to 29 from 31 percent while his disapproval rating was stable at 63 percent.
IPSOS found support for opposition Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin also dropped to 28 from 30 percent and his disapproval rating was unchanged at 57 percent.
IPSOS surveyed 957 people 18 and over on April 4 and 5.

The Harris poll also showed that 39 percent of voters would pick a candidate of the ruling centre-right if parliamentary elections were held next Sunday, against 26 percent who would choose an opposition Socialist.
The poll, of 1,002 adults questioned on April 4 and 5, also indicated that 15 percent would choose a far-right National Front candidate, 10 percent a Communist and eight percent an ecologist.
Elections to the National Assembly are due in March 1998, but Chirac has the power to call them earlier.
